text:
Adrian Kempe's season has come in two loud bursts with a lot of quiet in between. Two goals in Washington on Oct. 20, then five games without one, then a hat trick and an assist against San Jose on Wednesday in a 7-2 win, the night Yahoo Sports noted he passed Dustin Brown on the Kings' franchise list. NHL.com's headline called it his return.

The quiet stretch wasn't empty. He put 18 shots on net in those five games, and his chances this season add up to 6.88 expected goals (the quality of his looks) against six actual. That's a shooter getting roughly what he's earned. The Kings also control play with him out there: 57.7% of the 5v5 expected goals, about 13 points better than when he sits.

Our range has him around 36 goals and 75 points, the same 36 goals he scored last season. The caution comes from Evolving-Hockey, which had opponents creating more against him than against almost any forward in 2025-26 (bottom 5%). Watch whether this year's defensive numbers hold up.
headline: Kempe's goals arrive in bunches
